key.label: Four Choc Keys · R23
key.note: Fit the four Choc switches here. Choose Centre Click to fit the OP1 board and paddle.

steps.title: Snip Off the Print Pads
steps.caption: With the part cool, snip across the exposed middle of each narrow tie. Keep the cutter away from the permanent holder and clear the wire openings.

steps.title: Solder the Sockets Off the Holder
steps.caption: With the holder off the rod and upside down on the bench, solder each socket's two wires outside the holder. Keep solder on the terminal tabs, not above them.

steps.title: Slide In the Lower-Left Socket
steps.caption: Hold the socket about 2 mm below its seat and slide it in from the left edge, above the thin guard runners, wires trailing outward. Under its seat, lift it straight up so the two bosses enter the backplate.

steps.title: Slide In the Lower-Right Socket
steps.caption: Hold the socket about 2 mm below its seat and slide it in from the right edge, above the thin guard runners, wires trailing outward. Under its seat, lift it straight up so the two bosses enter the backplate.

steps.title: Push Up the Upper Sockets
steps.caption: Bring each socket up about 1 mm away from the rod position, so its inner solder joint passes beside the ring arm. 2 mm below the seat, move it in and press it up.

steps.title: Tape Every Socket
steps.caption: Lay one strip of polyimide tape across each socket and its wires onto the backplate, as on R16. Press the tape ends onto the backplate with a flat tool. Keep pressure off the guard runners. The tape insulates the solder from the rod and holds the socket.

steps.title: Press In the Switches
steps.caption: Back each socket from below with a finger or flat tool, then press each switch in from above until it clicks into the plate.

steps.title: Slide Onto the Rod
steps.caption: Slide the wired holder onto the rod end-first. The rod runs through the two rings behind the lower row; the guard has no ring of its own.

steps.title: Seated
steps.caption: Final position. The index finger rests on the rod between the inner runners; the runners sit under the lower sockets' outer terminals.

dfr.label: Centred OP1 click under the Grove touch board

board.label: OP1 PCB with two mounting eyelets

carrier.label: Key holder with two fixed hinge supports

cap.label: Orange Grove bracket and flexible hinge arms

housing.label: Fixed white socket beneath the board

steps.title: Remove Print Supports
steps.caption: Cut the narrow pad ties. Break the central support into small pieces and remove them through the empty PCB opening. Clear support inside the rod bore through its open rear end. Remove the outer finger-guard support outwards. Check the full rod bore, plug passage and cable passage are clear before fitting electronics or sliding the holder onto the rod.

steps.title: Plug In the OP1 Harness
steps.caption: Off the holder, connect the two-wire lead to the socket under the OP1 board. Keep the lead coming out from the end of the plug.

steps.title: Lower the Wired OP1 Board
steps.caption: Leave the upper keycaps off. Feed the lead through the opening, turn it beside the rod, then lower the board onto its two seats. Check the real lead can bend this way without being pinched or forced.

steps.title: Secure the Board
steps.caption: Fit the two kit screws through the eyelets. Tighten gently until the board stops moving.

steps.title: Seat the Mouse Switch
steps.caption: Line up the three terminals and press the switch flush into the sockets. Face the small plunger towards the three-key row.

steps.title: Refit the Upper Keycaps
steps.caption: Press the two upper keycaps onto their Choc stems.

steps.title: Bring the Bracket Over the Supports
steps.caption: Hold the touch-board bracket above the two fixed supports.

steps.title: Set the OP1 Stop Screw
steps.caption: Install the M2×4 socket-head screw from below before snapping the bracket in. Start 2¼ turns out from seated, then turn it in ⅛ turn at a time until the switch clicks and releases.

steps.title: Pinch the Bracket Arms
steps.caption: Hold the orange bracket above the holder. Pinch the two raised pads under the connector end so both tabs pull inwards.

steps.title: Lower Between the Supports
steps.caption: Keep pinching and lower the bracket. The two tabs pass between the two fixed supports.

steps.title: Let the Tabs Snap Into the Holes
steps.caption: Let go. Each arm springs back and its tab enters the hole in the support beside it.

steps.title: Seat the Grove Board
steps.caption: Two-key end at the top. Plug in the Grove cable first, feed the free wire ends through the left opening, then lower the gold face up onto the two centred seats.

steps.title: Fit the Two M2 Screws
steps.caption: Fasten the upper and lower tabs with two M2 × 4 mm pan-head screws. Tighten gently against the printed seats.

steps.title: Touch, Click and Release
steps.caption: Light contact on the gold pad sends touch to the XIAO. Press farther to click the separate OP1 switch, then release. The orange bracket pivots until its two feet meet the stops.

steps.title: Undo the Two Screws
steps.caption: Switch off first and leave slack in the cable. Remove both centred screws before lifting the module.

steps.title: Lift the Grove Board
steps.caption: Lift the Grove board with its cable still attached. Guide the loose wires back through the opening.

steps.title: Unplug the Grove Lead
steps.caption: Hold the board above the bracket. Release the latch and pull the plug down from its socket.

steps.title: Reconnect the Grove Lead
steps.caption: Line up the keyed plug and reconnect it above the bracket.

steps.title: Put the Grove Board Back
steps.caption: Feed the loose wire ends through the same opening before reseating the board.

steps.title: Fasten the Grove Board
steps.caption: Refit both screws and leave slack at the cable bend.

dfr.note: The OP1 board sits over the rod on a seat 0.9 mm higher than R37. The Grove board sits 2 mm to the left and 0.9 mm higher so its plug passes beside the OP1 board. The stop screw moves to the right of the board.

carrier.label: Key holder with two fixed hinge supports

steps.title: Pinch the Bracket Arms
steps.caption: Hold the orange bracket above the holder. Pinch the two raised pads under the connector end so both tabs pull inwards.

steps.title: Lower Between the Supports
steps.caption: Keep pinching and lower the bracket. The two tabs pass between the two fixed supports.

steps.title: Let the Tabs Snap Into the Holes
steps.caption: Let go. Each arm springs back and its tab enters the hole in the support beside it.

steps.title: Pinch to Release the Tabs
steps.caption: Pinch both pads. The tabs pull out of the support holes.

steps.title: Lift Off the Empty Bracket
steps.caption: Keep pinching and lift the bracket straight up.

steps.title: Pinch and Lower It Back
steps.caption: To refit, pinch again and lower the bracket between the supports.

steps.title: Let the Tabs Snap Back In
steps.caption: Let go so both tabs return into their holes.

xiao.label: XIAO holder · R25 lift-release trial
xiao.note: Fit the R25 holder and keeper together to try the stronger catch. The board sits in its original position.

keeper.label: R25 keeper and rounded lift tab

steps.title: Snip Off the Print Pads
steps.caption: With the part cool, snip across the exposed middle of each narrow tie. Keep the cutter away from the permanent holder and clear the wire openings.

steps.title: Lay In the Board
steps.caption: Tilt the near end of the board up about 6 degrees, slide the USB end under the two far fingers, then lower the near end onto its ledges. Side wires stay outside the walls. Underside solder must leave room: see the clearance map in geometry-checks.json.

steps.title: Point the Tooth Toward the Holder
steps.caption: Line up the two side ears with the grooves. The small tooth faces down and the rounded edge faces the board.

steps.title: Slide On the Keeper
steps.caption: Push along the grooves until the tab drops behind the ridge. The prongs rest over the two corners of the board.

steps.title: Slide the Rod Through the Rings
steps.caption: Feed the rod through both rings, end-first.

steps.title: Pull Gently to Check the Stop
steps.caption: A small straight pull brings the tooth against the steep face. The board prongs stay flat.

steps.title: Lift the Rounded Tab
steps.caption: Lift the rounded edge a little with a fingernail. The tooth rises above the ridge.

steps.title: Slide the Keeper Out
steps.caption: Keep the tab raised while you slide the keeper back along its two grooves.

steps.title: Let the Tab Settle
steps.caption: Let go once the tooth is clear. The spring tab returns to its flat shape.

steps.title: Lift the Board Out
steps.caption: Lift the keeper end of the board and slide the USB end out from under the far fingers.

steps.title: Slide the Holder Off the Rod
steps.caption: Draw the rod out through the rings to separate the holder.

xiao_latch.label: XIAO keeper latch · R25 cutaway
xiao_latch.note: Side section of the matching R25 parts. The bend is drawn from the checked CAD route.

holder.label: Blue holder ridge and steep face

keeper.label: Orange keeper tooth and spring tab

steps.title: Find the Ramp and Tooth
steps.caption: The orange spring is joined to the keeper outside this side section. The blue ridge has a slope on the way in and a steep face on the way out.

steps.title: Push Until It Clicks
steps.caption: The tooth climbs the blue slope. The tab drops flat once the tooth passes the steep face.

steps.title: Pull Gently to Check the Stop
steps.caption: A small straight pull brings the tooth against the steep face. The board prongs stay flat.

steps.title: Lift the Rounded Tab
steps.caption: Lift the rounded edge a little with a fingernail. The tooth rises above the ridge.

steps.title: Slide the Keeper Out
steps.caption: Keep the tab raised while you slide the keeper back along its two grooves.

steps.title: Let the Tab Settle
steps.caption: Let go once the tooth is clear. The spring tab returns to its flat shape.

battery.label: Battery holder · R22
battery.note: The cell is drawn at the manufacturer maximum envelope.

steps.title: Snip Off the Print Pads
steps.caption: With the part cool, snip across the exposed middle of each narrow tie. Keep the cutter away from the permanent holder and clear the wire openings.

steps.title: Insert the Cell
steps.caption: Slide the cell in, leads last. Bring the leads through the centre opening.

steps.title: Drop In the Door
steps.caption: Push the door straight down into its two slots until the centre tooth clicks under the lip. R22 has a longer lead-in at the slot tops, so the tooth is pushed aside more gradually. If it is still too stiff, use the trial door, which has a shallower tooth.

checks.note: Overlap near the bottom is the catch tooth flexing over the lip (designed snap), not a clash.

steps.title: Slide Onto the Rod
steps.caption: Slide the holder onto the rod end-first.

steps.title: Seated
steps.caption: Cell held by the walls and teeth without pressure; door latched.

battery_easy.label: Battery Holder · Easier Door
battery_easy.note: The cell is drawn at the manufacturer maximum envelope.

steps.title: Snip Off the Print Pads
steps.caption: With the part cool, snip across the exposed middle of each narrow tie. Keep the cutter away from the permanent holder and clear the wire openings.

steps.title: Insert the Cell

steps.title: Drop In the Door
steps.caption: Push the easier door straight down into the same slots. Its shallower centre tooth takes less force to fit and holds less firmly.

cable.label: Cable clip · 12 wires
cable.note: Clip frame: rod axis along Z, printed flat. Wire positions follow the stated 12 x 1.5 mm packing in parameters.json.

steps.title: Snip Off the Print Pads
steps.caption: With the part cool, snip across the exposed middle of each narrow tie. Keep the cutter away from the permanent holder and clear the wire openings.

steps.title: Slide the Clip Onto the Rod
steps.caption: Align the rod loop with a free rod end and slide the clip to position. Feed the wires through the slit in the second loop.

steps.title: Feed a Wire Through the Slit
steps.caption: Feed the flexible wires one at a time and move them aside to make room. This shows the last 1.5 mm wire entering with the rest already packed in the 7 mm loop.

steps.title: Seated
steps.caption: All twelve wires inside the loop. The clip guides the harness; it is not strain relief.
